cpc:titles.author_is_not_participant: Published jointly by the European Patent Office and the USPTO, patent offices rather than competition participants; the table is the classification standard the competition's own context codes refer to.

evidence.leakage: static source: no time axis, no temporal leakage path
evidence.snapshot: snapshot stable across two fetches: CPC-2024.01 (subset seeded 2026-08-03)

cpc:titles.expected_value: Pre-registered: replacing the bare CPC code with its official title text should help a text-pairing model that currently sees the context as an opaque token. Predicted effect on us-patent Pearson r: between +0.000 and +0.010, i.e. small but non-negative, judged against a no-external arm at matched budget. A negative effect would falsify the premise that the code is uninformative as a token.
cpc:titles.licence: Public classification scheme, published for free reuse by EPO and USPTO; no redistribution restriction on the code-title table.
cpc:titles.notes: First source of the lookup join key class: no time axis, so the leakage rule is 'static' rather than a lag. Admitted to prove the source layer generalizes past country-panel data.
cpc:titles.predates_competition: The CPC scheme has been published since 2013 and the cached vintage is CPC-2024.01; us-patent-phrase-to-phrase-matching opened 2022-03. The scheme predates the competition by ~9 years.
